title: Restore exact native-body acceptance through the shared Navigator

scope.subject: Prove a non-PlanetDefinition YEIS body keeps exact native identity from Chinese Search alias through shared destination execution and deep-link state

research_summary: Earth is correctly represented as a product PlanetDefinition, so the earlier Earth-native assertion had to be removed. That correction left the cloud suite without an independent exact-native-body case even though the product still supports moons, spacecraft and other YEIS bodies outside the React planet model. Reuse the existing exact-native-travel subsystem and the adopted Playwright browser suite. The Moon is a stable Solar System target: navigation.ts already curates Moon, Chinese aliases map 月球/月亮 to moon, and bridge.ts intentionally maps only planet/dwarf bodies into PlanetDefinition while moons remain native. One E2E case can therefore prove alias normalization, grouped Search, exact body:c0/moon destination identity, c0/moon camera target, native travel completion and shareable URL without adding production logic.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS remains the native universe/body identity and camera authority used by the existing exact-travel subsystem.
Playwright's auto-retrying locator assertions and expect.poll are the adopted way to verify asynchronous browser state without fixed arbitrary waits.
Playwright locator actions already auto-wait for actionability, so the acceptance case can use the actual Navigator controls rather than bypassing product interaction.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep pinned MIT YEIS as the native-body product authority; this unit validates the already-selected solution rather than adding another body model.
Reuse the existing Playwright Test browser harness and its retrying assertions/actionability instead of creating a custom runtime probe.
The already-adopted exact native travel adapter is the subsystem under acceptance; no alternate camera or coordinate path is introduced.
No additional component is needed; the acceptance path uses the real Navigator input/result/action elements and root runtime evidence.

candidates.name: Existing pinned YEIS exact native-body path
candidates.source: Current UniverseNavigationDestination plus YeisGalaxyScene native travel
candidates.reason: The production path already exists; the gap is explicit browser acceptance after Earth returned to product-world semantics.

candidates.name: Existing Playwright cloud browser acceptance
candidates.reason: Uses the same browser/runtime evidence and CI artifact pipeline already adopted for Search, Places, black holes, landmarks and deep links.

candidates.name: Custom native-body smoke script
candidates.reason: Would duplicate Playwright browser lifecycle, waiting, traces and failure diagnostics while bypassing the actual Navigator surface the user interacts with.

decision.rationale: Add no production path. Use the real Navigator with the existing Chinese alias map to select Moon, then assert the existing shared destination/native camera/deep-link contract through Playwright's retrying browser assertions.
decision.fallback: If Moon ever becomes a product PlanetDefinition, move this acceptance to another curated non-product native body such as a spacecraft rather than weakening exact-native-travel coverage.
